summary.en-US: Color-code and label Unqork builder components, see which Unqork environment you are on before you act, and inspect or edit page data with built-in debug tools.

description.en-US:
Unqlock makes the Unqork Config builder easier to read, tells you which environment you are working in, and adds debug tools for application pages.

**Component appearance**

- All 52 component types get their own color, icon and optional type label.
- Light and dark palettes, following the builder's own appearance.
- Separate switches for icon tints, left accents, full backgrounds and borders.
- Style the sidebar and the canvas independently, or turn styling off entirely.

**Environment awareness**

- A floating badge names the environment in its own color: STAGING, QA, UAT, PRE-PROD or PRODUCTION.
- Anything unrecognized stays UNKNOWN rather than being guessed.
- Visited Unqork hostnames are grouped into organizations automatically. Rename groups, correct labels, add your own domains, or switch discovery off.
- Switch links reopen the same path on another host in the same group.
- The production guard disables data edits and component execution on hosts you have marked as production.

**Debug tools**

- Log submission and cache data to the DevTools console, grouped or as one object.
- Add, update or remove a top-level submission property as text, a number or JSON.
- Execute a single component by its exact key.
- Every edit and execution asks for confirmation first, production is called out in that confirmation, and nothing runs automatically.

**Opening Unqlock**

Click the floating badge to open the whole menu inside the page, or use the toolbar button. The badge can sit in any corner, show the environment label or just the icon, or be switched off.

**Privacy**

Unqlock makes no external requests and collects no data. Appearance and environment preferences, including saved domain groups, are stored locally in the browser, and discovery records hostnames only, never paths, queries or page data. Debug tools use temporary access to the active tab rather than standing host permissions; opened from the badge, where no toolbar click is available to grant it, they ask for access to that one hostname, and the rest of the menu keeps working if you decline.

version.approval_notes: Unqlock is plain, unminified JavaScript, CSS and HTML with no bundler, minifier or runtime dependency. To reproduce this package: install Node.js 22, then run npm ci followed by npm run build. dist/firefox then contains exactly the files in this submission, and artifacts/unqlock-firefox.zip is the same package. The source archive includes the build scripts, tests and maintainer documentation in .claude/development.md.
